- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days < -0.3), reduce forecasted price by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) followed by a drop, cap the forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–3 days (especially in early forecast window), shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per lag day.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to align with mean reversion.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% to reflect diminishing momentum and avoid overconfidence in short-term trends.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model by 1–2% across multiple days, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to correct for underestimation bias.
